question.problem:
Consider the following matrices:

$$
C=[\begin{aligned}\pi  & 2\pi  \\ 0 & 2\pi \end{aligned}],\,D=[\begin{aligned}\pi  & 0 \\ 0 & 2\pi \end{aligned}],\,P=[\begin{aligned}1 & 2 \\ 0 & 1\end{aligned}]
$$

Given that $C=PD{P}^{-1},$ find $\operatorname{cos}⁡C.$
question.worked_solution:
Given a function $f$ and matrices $A$ and $S,$ where $S$ is invertible, we have

$$
f(SA{S}^{-1})=S\cdot f(A)\cdot {S}^{-1}.
$$

For $f(x)=\operatorname{cos}⁡C$ and the given matrix $C,$ we have

$$
\operatorname{cos}⁡C=\operatorname{cos}⁡(PD{P}^{-1})=P\cdot (\operatorname{cos}⁡D)\cdot {P}^{-1}.
$$

Now, since $D$ is a diagonal matrix, we get

$$
\operatorname{cos}⁡D=[\begin{aligned}\operatorname{cos}⁡\pi  & 0 \\ 0 & \operatorname{cos}⁡2\pi \end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}-1 & 0 \\ 0 & 1\end{aligned}].
$$

Also, the inverse of $P$ is

$$
{P}^{-1}=\frac{1}{1\cdot 1-2\cdot 0}[\begin{aligned}1 & -2 \\ 0 & 1\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}1 & -2 \\ 0 & 1\end{aligned}].
$$

Therefore, we conclude that

$$
\begin{aligned}\operatorname{cos}⁡C & =P\cdot (\operatorname{cos}⁡D)\cdot {P}^{-1} \\  & =[\begin{aligned}1 & 2 \\ 0 & 1\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}-1 & 0 \\ 0 & 1\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}1 & -2 \\ 0 & 1\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}1 & 2 \\ 0 & 1\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}-1 & 2 \\ 0 & 1\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}-1 & 4 \\ 0 & 1\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$
